title: CHEM1A Practice Quiz — Objective 2: Compounds & Nomenclature (DRAFT pending Gilley approval)

items.stem: Which compound is ionic even though it contains no metal?
items.explain: Ammonium (NH₄⁺) is a polyatomic cation, so NH₄Cl is a lattice of ions. 'Ionic requires a metal' is the misconception — the real test is whether the compound is built from ions.
BrCl is two nonmetals sharing electrons — molecular. The other three pair a metal with a nonmetal — ionic. Two different elements alone does not make a compound ionic.

items.stem: What is the formula of calcium phosphate?
items.explain: Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻: three +2 balance two −3 (both +6/−6) → Ca₃(PO₄)₂. The crisscross runs charge-to-subscript — Ca₂(PO₄)₃ is the crisscross run backward.

items.stem: An ionic compound has the formula X₂S. Which element could X be?
items.explain: S²⁻ balanced by two X means each X is +1 → Group 1 → lithium. Calcium and zinc form 2+ ions (giving XS); aluminum is 3+ (giving X₂S₃).

items.stem: What is the name of NiCl₂? (Nickel is a variable-charge metal.)
items.explain: Two Cl⁻ force Ni²⁺ → nickel(II) chloride. Variable-charge metals must state the charge; prefixes like di- belong to molecular naming.
K₂S is potassium sulfide — fixed-charge metal, -ide anion. Na₃P is sodium phosphide (phosphate is PO₄³⁻); Cu₂O is copper(I) oxide (one O²⁻ split across two Cu); ionic compounds never take prefixes.

items.stem: What is the name of SO₂?
items.explain: Molecular compound → prefixes count the atoms: sulfur dioxide. Roman numerals are for ionic compounds, and mono- is dropped on the first element.

items.stem: What is the formula of carbon disulfide?
items.explain: Di- on sulfide means two sulfur atoms; no prefix on carbon means one. Prefixes translate directly to subscripts.

items.stem: H₃PO₃(aq) contains the phosphite ion. Its name is:
items.explain: -ite anion → -ous acid: phosphite → phosphorous acid. -ate would give -ic (phosphoric); hydro- is reserved for binary acids with no oxygen.

items.stem: What is the formula of hypochlorous acid, formed from the hypochlorite ion (ClO⁻)?
items.explain: One H⁺ balances one ClO⁻ → HClO. The -ous/-ite pairing carries the oxygen count with it — no extra oxygens get added.

items.stem: Which compound is a carboxylic acid?
items.explain: The −COOH group (carbonyl + hydroxyl on the same carbon) defines a carboxylic acid. −OH alone is an alcohol; C−O−C is an ether.
Nitrogen bonded to carbon groups (no carbonyl attached) → amine. An amide requires the nitrogen attached to a C=O.

items.stem: What is the name of C₂H₆?
items.explain: Two carbons → eth-; C₂H₆ fits CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (all single bonds) → -ane. Ethene (C₂H₄) and ethyne (C₂H₂) have fewer hydrogens because of their multiple bonds.
Hex- = six carbons; -ene = one double bond; 1- puts it at the first carbon. CH₃(CH₂)₄CH₃ and C₆H₁₄ are hexane; the triple bond makes 1-hexyne.

items.stem: For an ionic compound, the term "formula unit" refers to:
choices: The smallest whole-number ratio of ions in the lattice
The total number of ions in one crystal
The sum of the atomic masses
items.explain: Ionic compounds are continuous lattices — there is no discrete molecule. The formula unit is the smallest neutral ratio, which is why 'molecule of NaCl' is imprecise.

items.stem: Two oxyanions of the same element differ by one oxygen: the ion with MORE oxygen takes the ending:
items.explain: -ate is the more-oxygen member of the pair (sulfate SO₄²⁻ vs sulfite SO₃²⁻). -ide marks simple monatomic anions; -ous is an acid ending, not an ion ending.
